session.title: Rain-day recovery gym plus clipless handling
session.purpose: Recover from Tuesday's hard 2K loop session while keeping movement quality and beginning low-risk clipless adaptation away from wet trails.

dose.readiness_basis: 2026-06-17 morning: yellow readiness, wake Body Battery 48, HRV unbalanced, ACWR 1.0 optimal.
dose.elliptical: 20-30 min easy, HR mostly 110-125 bpm, absolute cap 130 bpm.
dose.activation_weights: 10-15 min only: light squats or leg press, lunges, hip hinge, row/fly, and core/bracing. Use 1-2 easy sets; leave 4+ reps in reserve.
dose.clipless_drill: Optional 10-20 min later only on a dry, flat, low-traffic condo area or sheltered car-park space.
dose.clipless_drill_cap: Skill practice only: no hills, no torque, no sprints, no wet paint, no traffic, no fatigue.
dose.hard_cap: Total Garmin training load under 40. If elliptical plus weights already feel like work, skip the bike drill.

session.adaptation_hypothesis: Low-intensity circulation and light activation should improve recovery from Tuesday's 215-load session while controlled clipless repetitions reduce equipment-risk without adding meaningful physiological strain.
execution_rules: Keep the gym session restorative; breathing should stay controlled throughout.
Use activation weights for range, control, and posture, not strength stimulus.
For clipless, rehearse start-stop, one-foot release, emergency release, and slow turns before riding continuous loops.
Use a wall, railing, or sheltered flat space for initial repetitions if the ground is wet.
If unclipping feels delayed or uncertain, stop before fatigue teaches bad timing.

expected_result.next_day: Better recovery signal and no trail-quality penalty for Friday/Saturday.

stop_rules: Stop elliptical if HR rises above 130 bpm at easy effort or legs feel heavy.
Stop weights if any set creates burn, strain, or soreness risk.
Skip outdoor clipless practice if surfaces remain wet/slippery or traffic is present.
Stop clipless practice after any awkward near-fall, delayed unclipping, or rising frustration.
